description: Olá! Meu nome é Maria Eduarda e sou veterana neste evento. Minha paixão é transformar ciência, tecnologia e astronomia em soluções reais desta vez, com uma equipe dedicada a destacar o protagonismo das mulheres na ciência. Procura um desafio de alto nível e ritmo acelerado? Junte-se a mim!
summary:
We developed AstroHealth, a space health ecosystem integrated with Cosmo, an artificial intelligence agent trained on medical and mission data to support astronauts in real time. The solution includes interfaces for smartwatches, an onboard medical dashboard, and an app for family members on Earth.
The project addresses the challenge of deep-space health, where spaceflight affects multiple body systems simultaneously and communication delays between the crew and doctors on Earth take 3 to 22 minutes (such as in missions to Mars). To overcome this critical wait time, Cosmo continuously monitors vital signs, spacecraft sensors, periodic medical exams, and pre-mission health history. Upon detecting anomalies compared to the astronaut's individual baseline, the AI issues alerts, validates symptoms with the crew member, notifies the medical team, and guides the crew until a doctor can intervene.
AstroHealth is essential for identifying silent and severe risks such as asymptomatic blood clots in flight and severe post-landing blood pressure drops as well as filling historical gaps in space data, offering personalized monitoring especially relevant to the health of female astronauts on long-duration missions.

Below is the link to the AI on GitHub:  https://github.com/KamyllaJawad/nexus-saturn.git
details: In deep-space missions, such as to the Moon and Mars, the extreme environment overloads multiple systems of the human body at the same time, yet a medical emergency faces a critical obstacle: the communication signal between the spacecraft and doctors on Earth can take 3 to 22 minutes to arrive. To address this vulnerability without replacing the medical team, we developed AstroHealth, a space health ecosystem guided by Cosmo, an artificial intelligence agent trained on clinical and mission data that works alongside the crew during these decisive minutes. Integrating pre-mission history, spacecraft sensors, periodic exams, and biometrics captured by smartwatches, the system tracks each astronaut's individual baseline. Upon detecting any anomaly, such as a sudden change in blood pressure or signs of silent conditions like asymptomatic blood clots in flight Cosmo issues immediate alerts, validates symptoms with the crew member, notifies doctors on Earth, and guides onboard procedures until the official response arrives, while also keeping family members informed through a dedicated app. More than just a rapid-response tool, AstroHealth brings an essential and historically overlooked perspective to space medicine by personalizing monitoring for female astronauts, who represent about 15% of space travelers and face specific risks, such as a higher incidence of in-flight injuries and post-landing bone density loss. With a viable architecture focused on the future of human exploration, AstroHealth ensures that no matter how far humanity goes, no astronaut faces a medical emergency alone.
